chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: When a man makes a vow from his wife, which is that he says 'By Allah, I will not have intercourse with you for such and such [period]', and he says 'By Allah, I will anger you', then he angers her, then he waits for her for four months. If he returns (to normalcy), and returning is that he reconciles with his family or divorces her at that time, and a divorce does not occur between them until it is suspended. If it is also after four months until he returns or is divorced.

key_terms.إِيلَاء: A vow by a husband to abstain from sexual intercourse with his wife

ai.seo_question: What is the duration and procedure for a husband's vow of abstention (Ila) from his wife in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies the specific duration and conditions of 'Ila', a vow of abstention where the husband swears not to consummate the marriage. It highlights the scholarly distinction that the divorce is not immediate but suspended for four months, allowing the husband to either reconcile (by resuming intimacy) or finalize the separation, reflecting the juristic principle of giving the couple a grace period before permanent dissolution.
